name: Azha
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. A Phula Comparative Lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International. 144 pp.
catalog_locator: sec. 3.5 'Azha phonology in brief', pp. 10-12; syllable-template statement p. 10, tone paragraph p. 12.
catalog_quote: In all Azha syllable templates, a vowel, or segment with high sonority, and a contrastive tone are obligatory. Two Azha tonemes have been noted to regularly feature tense voice phonation in all varieties in all varieties I have personally researched. ... Azha features five tone contrasts. Three register tonemes are produced using modal voice: high-level /44/, mid-level /33/ and low-level /22/. Two contour tonemes are coarticulated with tense voice phonation: high-rising /45/ and low-falling /21/. ... A sixth marginal toneme low-rising /13/ has been noted to occur on certain Chinese loans. In the Azha dialect represented in the comparative lexicon, the /45/ toneme is often produced as modal register [55] by younger generation speakers – thus making for four level tones contrasts. ... Although sandhi phenomena were infrequently encountered in the Azha data, /45+45/ was usually noted to yield either [44-44] or [55-44]. Another, more complex process is also of note, such that /33+22+33+22/ yields a [33-34-33-22] pattern.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Azha is a syllable-tone language: every syllable carries one of five contrastive tonemes (three modal level tones 44/33/22, two tense-voice contour tones 45/21), with limited tone sandhi. The sketch makes no statement about word stress or accent at all. The only accent-typological classification found, Iwasa et al. 2017 (SAG 7, p. 14, saved), places Azha in type 'C-1 ST+YL' (syllable tone + distinctive phonation), not in the 'stress accent' or 'pitch accent' types.
new_statements.exceptions: None about stress. Tone: marginal sixth toneme /13/ on Chinese loans; /45/ often modal [55] for younger speakers (LJY); sandhi /45+45/ -> [44-44]/[55-44], /33+22+33+22/ -> [33-34-33-22]; dialectal {(C)V(V)T} and reported {(C)V(V)T(P)} templates (Gaodeng, per Wu 1996).
new_statements.domain_note: Tone description is of monomorphemic citation forms and short compounds (sandhi) from elicited wordlist data of Azha-LJY (Luojiayi, Binglie Township, Wenshan County); no phrase-level prosody discussed. The quote is a tone statement, not a stress statement: the source is silent on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Pelkey's Azha data (the quoted sketch) are from Azha-LJY, Luojiayi village, Binglie Township, Wenshan County (with notes on Xiaopingba XPB and Huangzhai dialects, and Gaodeng GDC after Wu 1996); Iwasa's Azha (2003, 2004) is from Madi village, Dongshan Township, Wenshan County (阿札彝語); Lama 2012 uses 'Azha' to cover Azha and Pu [phu21] of Wenshan Prefecture. All are the language-level glottocode azha1235 (no dialect glottocodes exist).

sources.note: p. 14, sec. C 'Tone/accent + phonation patterns': 'C-1 ST+YL / LB: Lisu, Hani, Azha, Atsi, Langsu, etc.' i.e. Azha is classified as a syllable-tone language with phonologically distinctive phonation; the scheme has separate types 'A-4 Stress accent (SA)' and 'A-3 Pitch accent (PA)' into which Azha is not placed. Survey-level classification (525 TB lects), per-language sources not given.

sources.note: Examines pathways to rising tones in Ngwi (Loloish); among the 11 Ngwi language clusters examined, a new rising tone value developed unambiguously from a historically high tone in nine; argues *high > rising is a recurrent phonetic tone change alongside consonant-induced rising. Azha contributes Proto-Ngwi tone-class reflexes (dataset shows /44 33 22 21 45/-type values from Pelkey 2011); no first-hand Azha tone analysis.
